jobs.title: Install the Chief relay on the Mini
jobs.body:
Install the Chief relay on the Mini (Ben asked for it, 7 Oct; AGENTS.md "Chief relay"). Free; nothing on YouTube.

    cd ~/YouTube/orbit-with-ben && git pull
    mkdir -p ~/_desk/bin ~/_desk/state && cp scripts/chief_relay.py ~/_desk/bin/
    cp scripts/mini/com.owb.chief-relay.plist ~/Library/LaunchAgents/
    launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.owb.chief-relay.plist
    python3 ~/_desk/bin/chief_relay.py status

Then check, and put each result in the done note:
- `status` shows Cursor UP and, if Codex is installed, Codex UP. Grok shows down until it runs jobs.py.
- `codex exec --help` lists `--full-auto`, `--add-dir` and `-c`. If a flag is missing, set CODEX_FLAGS in the plist
  (an EnvironmentVariables dict) to what this version accepts, and say what you set.
- If a ~/_desk/state/cursor-covers-chief file exists from the old worker, delete it. It does nothing now.
- After the first run, the end of ~/Library/Logs/chief-relay.log.

**Ben's notes on 025 v03c (board tick, 8 Oct 22:39).** He wants two changes. Make **v03d** from the v03c build, and change nothing else.

1. **2:54 "This image looks bad."** That's cut 39, row 14, 170.73–175.97 s: PIA12337, the CAD "Computer Reconstruction of Spirit Predicament". It's a flat brown background, 1094 px wide and upscaled 1.84×.

   - If PIA12102 can't fill 16:9 at an upscale of 2.35× or less, use **PIA12205** (HiRISE, "Orbital View of Spirit at Troy").
   - Same timing; still_motion push; jitter ≤ 0.35 px; fill and polish gates PASS for the new cut. Drop PIA12337 from the long.
2. **"Are we sure we have not used this background music before?"** Ben's right. v03c's bed is `OWB UAT/jupiter-music.mp3`, the same bed the 023 and 024 cuts use. Every earlier film (013, 021, 022) had its own `<film>_score_bed_v01`.
   - Make 025's own bed with `04_Audio/tools/generate_music_bed.py` (ElevenLabs API; no website generation): `--project mars-robot --length-ms 500000 --out-dir 02_Video-Projects/025_Could-A-Robot-Survive-On-Mars/05_Music`.
   - Prompt (pass as `--prompt`): "Instrumental cinematic space documentary underscore for Orbit with Ben, Mars robot film. Cold dusty red plains and a small machine that refuses to stop: lonely, patient, quietly brave, with a slow ache as the power fades. Soft low strings, muted felt piano, warm analog pads, sparse mechanical ticks kept very quiet, thin wind texture. NOT Jupiter music, NOT Saturn ring chimes, NOT Moon Leaving lunar piano, NOT Sun golden strings. Vast quiet scale, room for British narration. Pace: 60-72 BPM, slow and steady under the narration, the low strings lifting only for the Opportunity farewell. No vocals, no drums, no EDM, no trailer hit."
   - **Credit guard.** Read ElevenLabs credits left first. Don't generate if fewer than 30,000 would be left afterwards (voice work comes first). Instead, block this job with "music bed: needs Claude's call on credits".
   - After generating, record credits before and after in `04_Audio/elevenlabs_ledger.jsonl` (stem `mars-robot_score_bed_v01`). One generation only. If it sounds wrong, post it; don't re-roll.
   - Mix exactly as v03c (≈ −14 LUFS, bed under the VO, music for the full runtime, fade at the end).
3. **Deliver:**
   - `OWB UAT/025_MarsRobot_full_rough_v03d.mp4`;
   - **`OWB UAT/025_MarsRobot_v03d_PHONE.mp4`**, the same phone encode as J0067 (it's the file Ben opens), and confirm it's uploaded;
   - a pack with the new cut's frame and the gates.
4. Post on #99 for Claude's check. Don't delete or move anything in OWB UAT.

   - `python3 scripts/picture_qa.py <v03d.mp4> --cuts cuts_v03d.json --pool nasa_pool_v01.json --out-dir <pack>` must PASS;

Fill 16:9, no Orbit at frame 0. Update `frame0_sheet`.

So when you look towards Proxima, you are seeing light that left it more than four years ago."* The cut shows `journey`, the three-line walk/car/jet race, which belongs to row 24. **2. At 6:02–6:18 (row 27, `lighttimes`).** The VO says: *"Moonlight reaches you in just over a second. Sunlight takes about eight minutes. Light from the nearest star takes more than four years, and that is the shortest trip of its kind there is."* Bars on a log scale read as a chart; a viewer can't tell what they are. - **New code graphic `lightrace`, text-free, timed to each sentence:** a small real-photo Earth disc on the right, and on the left, in turn, the real source as a cut-out disc on black space (no box):

Proxima's pulse sets out and is still only a sliver of the way across when the sentence ends, then holds on that slow progress over "the shortest trip of its kind there is".
